original.Body: Paul got a box of 457 erasers and 617 crayons for his birthday. At the end of the school year he only had 523 crayons left while not having lost a single eraser.
original.Question: How many more crayons than erasers did he have left?

thoughts.current:
Step 1: Calculate the number of crayons Paul used or lost during the school year.
Paul started with 617 crayons and had 523 left at the end of the year. So, he used or lost:
617 - 523 = 94 crayons

Step 2: Since Paul did not lose any erasers, he still has the same number of erasers as he started with, which is 457.

Step 3: To find out how many more crayons than erasers Paul has left, subtract the number of erasers from the number of crayons he has left:
523 (crayons left) - 457 (erasers) = 66

Answer: Paul has 66 more crayons than erasers left.
